edit.description: In jobStatus's per-job map (~L458), catch a non-ENOENT readPendingLoose throw per-job (mirror the existing null/'unparsable' convention) instead of letting it escape the whole enumeration — matches this file's own JobStatus.pending doc comment and spec/jobs.md's 'one broken plan never hides the others'.
Cover a multi-job jobStatus() call where one job's pending.json read fails non-ENOENT: that job's row reads unparsable, sibling jobs still list normally.

summary: e9e2864's readPendingLoose rethrow escapes jobStatus's per-job map — one job's non-ENOENT pending.json read failure now aborts flume job status for every job
tests: jobStatus(repoRoot) returns every job's row when exactly one job's pending.json read fails non-ENOENT; the failing job's own row reads as unparsable, sibling jobs are unaffected
acceptance: A non-ENOENT pending.json read failure for one job under .flume/jobs/ never removes sibling jobs from flume job status output
notes: Found sweeping src/job.ts (stamp 8312b25). e9e2864 made readPendingLoose rethrow non-ENOENT failures; jobStatus's per-job map has no per-job catch, so one job's throw escapes the whole enumeration — runJobVerb's try/catch (cli.ts) wraps the aggregate call, not each job. Contradicts JobStatus.pending's own doc comment and spec/jobs.md's 'one broken plan never hides the others'. tests/job.test.ts:1211 pins the single-job-throws shape but never covers siblings.
